name: gpt-oss
what: Chat template of gpt-oss (the harmony response format).

upstream.license_evidence: LICENSE file in the repository at this revision (Apache License 2.0) and the card's license: apache-2.0
upstream.copyright: The upstream LICENSE leaves the appendix's copyright line unfilled.

checks: Byte-identical to upstream: chat_template.jinja in openai/gpt-oss-20b at revision 6cee5e81ee83 equals the text (go run ./tools/feedbuild upstream re-checks it). Last checked 2026-10-14.

Socair's chat-template check (defilantech/socair@ddfe650b5f50, the RealTemplates corpus gate, 2026-10-14): PASS, with no code reach and no content-conditional injection; rendered 6 of 6 probe conversations (2 trigger probes refused: the template raises an error, by design, when message content carries <|channel|> tags); text it adds of its own: a system message naming the model ("You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI." unless model_identity is given), its knowledge cutoff, the current date (strftime_now), and the reasoning effort; the tools namespace rendered as TypeScript-like declarations; channel and recipient markers; nothing is added under a content condition.
notes: Harmony layout (<|start|>role<|message|>...<|end|>, with analysis, commentary, and final channels). Always writes a system message with identity, dates, and reasoning effort; a user's system message becomes a developer message. Tool schemas are rendered as TypeScript-style function declarations, and builtin_tools can add browser and python tool descriptions. Message text is tested only to refuse <|channel|> tags in content or thinking, which raises an exception instead of adding text. The file is a standalone chat_template.jinja with no trailing newline; the tokenizer_config.json at this revision has no chat_template field.

review.means: A person read the whole template text at the pinned revision and confirmed that it only lays out the conversation it is given: it adds no instruction to the model beyond the publisher's own default system prompt and tool scaffolding, no branch adds text when a message contains a particular string, and it reaches nothing but the documented chat-template variables and filters. Byte identity with the upstream file and Socair's chat-template check are mechanical checks, listed under checks; they are not the review.
